# Psalm 142 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-maskil of-David when-he-was in-the-cave. A-prayer. With-my-voice to-YHWH I-cry; with-my-voice to-YHWH I-plead.

**2** I-pour-out before-him my-complaint; my-distress before-him I-declare.

**3** When-faints upon-me my-spirit, and-you know my-path. In-the-way which I-walk they-have-hidden a-trap for-me.

**4** Look to-the-right and-see — there-is-no for-me one-recognizing; has-perished refuge from-me; there-is-no one-caring for my-soul.

**5** I-have-cried to-you O-YHWH; I-have-said, 'You my-refuge, my-portion in-land-of the-living.'

**6** Attend to-my-cry for I-am-brought-very-low; deliver-me from-my-persecutors, for they-are-too-strong for-me.

**7** Bring-out from-prison my-soul, to-give-thanks to-your-name; around-me will-crown the-righteous, for you-will-deal-bountifully with-me.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **142:4**: 'There-is-no one-recognizing... no one-caring for my-soul' — the nadir of isolation; David in the cave with no human ally.

- **142:5**: 'You my-refuge, my-portion' — when all human refuge has perished, God himself becomes both shelter and inheritance.

— EMET
